LESSON: MAPS AND MAP WORK

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Natural and Historic Built Environments in Africa
Topic 4.3: Maps and map work
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Maps and map work, part of Natural and Historic Built Environments in Africa in Grade 7 SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How are maps used? 2. Why is time different in various locations?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. brainstorm on the position, shape, and size of Africa and share in class,

2. buzz on the countries that make up Africa and display in class,

3. draw an outline map of Africa creatively and indicate the countries that make up Africa and display it in class,

4. use relevant print media or digital devices to establish the position and location of places and features on a map,

5. calculate the time of different places using longitudes,

6. discuss and appreciate positive features that are associated with Africa. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. brainstorm on the position, shape, and size of Africa and share in class,
2. buzz on the countries that make up Africa and display in class,
3. draw an outline map of Africa creatively and indicate the countries that make up Africa and display it in class,
4. use relevant print media or digital devices to establish the position and location of places and features on a map,
5. calculate the time of different places using longitudes,
6. discuss and appreciate positive features that are associated with Africa. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Maps and map work together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital Literacy: learners apply the skill of designing and creating new digital artefacts, content, and materials as they

establish the position and location of places and features on a map.

● Creativity and Imagination: learners undertake group activities and exchange new ideas that inspire creative thinking as

they draw an outline map of Africa.

Values:
● Responsibility: learners develop diligence as they research the three types of maps used in Social Studies and make

summary notes.

● Patriotism: learners develop loyalty as they draw an outline map of Africa and indicate the countries that makeup Africa.

● Unity: learners demonstrate fairness as they brainstorm the position, shape, and size of Africa.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Social Cohesion: learners brainstorm on the position, shape, and size of Africa.

● Environmental Education: learners use latitudes to locate the position of places and features on a map.

Link to other Subjects:

● Learners apply calculation skills as they use longitudes to calculate the time of different places in the world.
